proposed.text: Under SPP 207, must the Architect retain a distinct professional identity as defined in SPP 200?

options.text: No, the architect becomes a contractor in design-build and loses professional identity
No, the design-build framework supersedes SPP 200 and establishes a new identity
Yes, the Architect must retain distinct professional identity per SPP 200
Yes, but only when operating under DBS-GMPCC delivery method specifically

rationale.a: The architect never becomes a contractor. Professional identity must be maintained.
rationale.b: SPP 207 does not supersede SPP 200. The foundational principles remain.
rationale.c: Correct. Even in design-build, the Architect must retain their distinct professional identity as defined in SPP 200, maintaining the distinction between professional practice and contracting.
rationale.d: The requirement applies to all design-build arrangements, not just GMPCC.
rationale.correct: SPP 207 requires the Architect to retain distinct professional identity as defined in SPP 200, even when providing design-build services. This ensures the architect maintains professional standards, ethical obligations, and legal responsibilities regardless of delivery method.
rationale.takeaway: Architect must retain professional identity in design-build — always per SPP 200.
